name: San Luís Temalacayuca Popoloca
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Con la excepción de algunos adverbios y palabras onomatopéyicas, todos los sustantivos, verbos, adjetivos y adverbios tienen un acento fijo en la sílaba con la penúltima mora. Ya que la cantidad vocálica es contrastiva, puede haber tres patrones de la cantidad vocálica y el acento (ˈVV#, ˈV$V# y ˈVV$V#). Cuando el acento cae en la penúltima vocal corta con una consonante o secuencia consonántica (ˈVCV#), la porción consonántica se alarga fonéticamente ([ˈVCCV]). [...] El acento se desplaza hacia la derecha por sufijación o composición. Los enclíticos son extramétricos y se escriben separados en la ortografía.
new_statements.translation: With the exception of some adverbs and onomatopoeic words, all nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs have a fixed stress on the syllable with the penultimate mora. Since vowel length is contrastive, there can be three patterns of vowel length and stress (ˈVV#, ˈV$V# and ˈVV$V#). When the stress falls on a penultimate short vowel followed by a consonant or consonant sequence (ˈVCV#), the consonantal portion is phonetically lengthened ([ˈVCCV]). [...] Stress moves to the right under suffixation or compounding. Enclitics are extrametrical and are written separately in the orthography.

The quoted passage is at printed pp. 110-111 (PDF pp. 6-7), section 'Características generales de la lengua' > 'Esbozo fonológico', last paragraph of p. 110 running onto p. 111, exactly as quoted apart from line-break hyphenation (to-dos, sí-laba, pue-de, conso-nante, alar-ga, com-posición) and the reader's explicit '[...]' eliding the sentence 'Una palabra monomoraica sin alguna palabra antecedente dentro de una frase, se apoya con la realización del acento en una i-protética (%ˈi-CV#).' The same section also says 'La cantidad vocálica está anclada por el acento' (p. 109) and that the only coda consonants '…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is fixed on the syllable that contains the penultimate mora, counted from the right edge of the word. Since vowel length is contrastive (long vowel = two moras; coda ʔ/y/w are non-moraic), a word-final long vowel is stressed (ˈVV#), otherwise the penultimate syllable is stressed (ˈV$V#, ˈVV$V#). This is a right-edge, quantity-sensitive (moraic-trochee-like) rule rather than syllabic penult stress: final syllable stressed iff it has a long vowel. Long vowels are only allowed under stress; when suffixation or compounding moves stress rightward, the formerly stressed long vowel is shortened (with tone deletion). Monomoraic words in isolation take a stressed prothetic i- (bimoraic minimum).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any of the three sources opened (Tlalocan 2016, ICUWPL 2017, LSJ 2016).
new_statements.exceptions: 'algunos adverbios y palabras onomatopéyicas' are excepted from the rule; enclitics are extrametrical; unnativized Spanish loans keep a fixed tonal-length template (…V)V́V' (e.g. jusée' 'hoz'), whose final long vowel takes stress in accordance with the mora rule (footnote 8 notes that in Otlaltepec, not Temalacayuca, such loans have shortened to final-stressed jusé').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in the lexical word (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs), including suffixes and compounds (stress moves rightward when these are added); enclitics are extrametrical and outside the domain. A phrase-level adjustment: a monomoraic word with no preceding word in the phrase (i.e. in isolation/citation form) gets a stressed prothetic i- to satisfy a bimoraic minimum. The ICUWPL 2017 paper adds that a long vowel that loses stress is shortened with tone deletion, i.e. vowel length is licensed by stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All three opened sources describe exactly the variety of San Luis Temalacayuca, municipio de Tepanco de López, Puebla (ISO pps, Glottolog sanl1248), from the author's own fieldwork 2013–2016; Nakamoto's own dialect grouping is Temalacayuca vs. Tlacoyalco (sanm1301) vs. 'Southwestern Popoloca' (all other lects). Note: Glottolog ref 588760 types Nakamoto 2016 'The Morphology of Person...' as a master's thesis, but the author's CV and his Tlalocan 2016 bibliography call it a BA thesis (tesis de licenciatura, TUFS); his UNAM MA thesis (2020) is on Ayautla Mazatec and his UNAM PhD (2026) on Lalana Chinantec, neither on Popoloca.

sources.note: pp. 110–111 ('Esbozo fonológico'): except for some adverbs and onomatopoeia, all nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs have fixed stress on the syllable containing the penultimate mora; because vowel length is contrastive this yields three patterns ˈVV#, ˈV$V#, ˈVV$V#; in ˈVCV# the consonant is phonetically lengthened; a monomoraic word without a preceding word in the phrase takes a stressed prothetic i-; stress shifts rightward under suffixation or compounding; enclitics are extrametrical.

sources.citation: Nakamoto, Shun. 2017. "On the Underlying Representation of Creaky Vowels in Temalacayuca Popoloca". ICU Working Papers in Linguistics 2: 59–65. doi:10.34577/00004242 (International Christian University repository).
sources.note: p. 59 (§1.2): "Stress is fixed on the syllable with the penultimate mora; therefore, final syllable is stressed in VV# while the penultimate in VCV# (with phonetic lengthening of C) or VVCV#. The stress shifts due to suffixation; losing the stress, the lexical long vowel is contracted, accompanied with tone deletion and (in case of interrupted vowels) glottal stop resyllabification." Also: phrase-initial word must be minimally bimoraic, so monomoraic words in isolation get prothetic ī-. Three level tones H/M/L per mora.

sources.citation: 中本舜 (Nakamoto, Shun). 2016. ポポロカ語テマラカユカ方言における2種の名詞複合 [Two types of noun compounding in the Temalacayuca dialect of Popoloca]. 日本言語学会第152回大会予稿集 (Proceedings of the 152nd Meeting of the Linguistic Society of Japan), paper F-3, pp. 222–227.
sources.note: p. 223 (§1.2): 「プロミネンス位置は固定で、最後から2番目のモーラが属する音節に付与される。つまり、ˈμ.μ#, ˈμμ.μ#, ˈμμ# が可能なプロミネンスと母音長のパタンである。」 ('The prominence position is fixed: it is assigned to the syllable to which the penultimate mora belongs; i.e. ˈμ.μ#, ˈμμ.μ#, ˈμμ# are the possible prominence/vowel-length patterns.') Long vowels are allowed only in the prominent syllable and are contracted when prominence moves; syllable-final ʔ is non-moraic.
